thread.title: Apple: Even Bulls Must Acknowledge A Tough Upcoming 2019 - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

author: Michael Boyd
title: Apple: Even Bulls Must Acknowledge A Tough Upcoming 2019 - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
As a holder for more than a decade, watching long-term Apple ( AAPL ) shareholders leave money on the table has been a frustrating endeavor. When I last covered Apple ( AAPL ) in September of last year (“ Apple: Some Bearish Skepticism Is Needed ”) I cautioned that trading multiples were getting lofty and the market was giving investors an opportunity to hedge. I got quite a bit of flak for that recommendation – I usually do on research reports like these – yet here we are a few months later: shares peaked in early October and the price has fallen off a proverbial cliff since then. Given the price action, I wanted to revisit the data I presented originally, share an update, and also illustrate how I believe Apple will trade over the next year – and what investors should do about it.
Other authors take a different mindset on this; Michael Wiggins De Oliveira says to “Follow Warren Buffet and act by doing nothing”. I take a structurally different approach. Most Seeking Alpha investors are running portfolios substantially smaller than Warren Buffet… by many orders of magnitude. Buffett cannot be dynamic. By that, I mean he cannot sell or hedge without materially shifting markets – even in Apple. At this stage, the Berkshire portfolio is pigeonholed into his “buy and hold forever” strategy. As a small fish in one of the most liquid stocks out there, those reading this are not in the same situation. Take advantage of that.
So, rather than regurgitate many of the same talking points (iPhone in China issue, 2019 guidance cut, lengthening upgrade cycle, Apple stretching out average selling prices (“ASPs”)) that most people should be more than worn out, I wanted to reinforce a couple of small points today:
Historically, Apple still isn’t cheap on a free cash flow basis. This has plenty of room to fall further. Apple is going to roll into some very tough comps from revenue decline and lapping tax reform. Implied volatility is above most of 2018 levels sans December; hedging looks fairly attractive.
As I did in September, I think investors have an option to take some risk off the table in a controlled manner to reduce portfolio volatility before Apple heads into strength. Hedging through the first nine months of 2019 appears prudent before the picture improves.
The Case For Hedging
This chart should look familiar to those that read my last research note. The data is the same, just updated for the recent sell-off. This maps out free cash flow and free cash flow excluding working capital impact against market; better known as free cash flow yield. Pretty clear takeaway from this is on the advantages of buying low, and selling high and it also gives some insight on the value today. While there have been quite a few “buy the dip” calls here on Seeking Alpha, Apple is only around “average” cheapness on a historical basis today.
Yes, this is a backwards-looking snapshot however Apple should generate roughly similar cash flow figures in fiscal 2019 versus 2018 despite the guidance cut and growth headaches from a slip in iPhone unit sales. Based on my models, that lowered Q1 guidance points to about a ~13% dip in iPhone revenue versus fiscal Q1 2018; other segments by comparison will continue to see feverish growth (consistent with lowered guidance which ~8% off at the midpoint).
Yes, Apple has faced all of these headaches before. Long term bulls have gone through this many times over the years – there is not much new in the 2019 bear case versus 2015 or 2013. Still, fiscal 2019 comps look tough and it will be an obstacle:
In my opinion, multiple expansion in this kind of environment is unlikely. Most companies have a hard time posting substantial share price growth within an environment where they are dealing with tough year over year and sequential comps. Despite tailwinds from the Apple buyback program driving earnings per share, most of Apple’s quarterly comps are going to be tough this coming year, particularly after fiscal Q1. 2018 was aided by tax reform tailwinds (still the case for fiscal Q1) but after that the story gets much more complicated.
In my view, an Apple pricing recovery is much more likely to take place in the back half of the year when we get more visibility into fiscal 2020 phone and accessory offerings (including some potential new products) and news on 5G. That is the positive sentiment driver. Fiscal 2020 will also see Services revenue climb to above 40% of gross profit as management executes on its long term goal of doubling fiscal 2016 Services revenue by that time. The FASB revenue recognition standard, which will move revenue out of the Product bucket and into Services, will also help drive this. Bulls have been clamoring for a revaluation of Apple more in-line with peers like Microsoft ( MSFT ) or Google (NASDAQ: GOOGL ) ( GOOG ) for a very long time; in my opinion that will not happen until Services chunks out a bigger portion of consolidated gross profit and management starts presenting more data on Services. Until then, that above trailing free cash flow model (as well as projecting out future free cash flow) remains gospel. Don’t expect multiple expansion outside of the historic trading range.
That brings us to hedging. For longs – especially the income-focused crowd here – that means covered calls as a preferred method.
*Source: Author calculations. Option premiums vary wildly, check pricing before entering any trades.
We can have an all-day debate on whether to go at the money, out of the money, or how long out into the future to go versus rolling shorter terms. Everyone has their own personal approach that they take to options that they feel comfortable with. Personally, I find the four contracts above appealing based on time of expiry and premium realized.
In my view, especially heading into a rough 2019 given continued Chinese worries and near-recessionary economic indicators in Europe, there is a lot of value in taking a little risk off the table today and locking in some upside.
